You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 5e29d1443c46b6ca70a4c940a67e8c09f05dcb7e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Michael Guralnik <michaelgur@mellanox.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Feb 2020 13:38:34 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/mlx5: Prevent UMR usage with RO only when we have RO
 caps

Relaxed ordering is not supported in UMR so we are disabling UMR usage
when user passes relaxed ordering access flag.

Enable using UMR when user requested relaxed ordering but there are no
relaxed ordering capabilities.

This will prevent user from unnecessarily registering a new mkey.

Fixes: d6de0bb1850f ("RDMA/mlx5: Set relaxed ordering when requested")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200227113834.94233-1-leon@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Michael Guralnik <michaelgur@mellanox.com>
Reviewed-by: Maor Gottlieb <maorg@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/mlx5_ib.h b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/mlx5_ib.h
index d9bffcc93587..f21d446249b8 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/mlx5_ib.h
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/mlx5_ib.h
@@ -1532,7 +1532,9 @@ static inline bool mlx5_ib_can_use_umr(struct mlx5_ib_dev *dev,
 	    MLX5_CAP_GEN(dev->mdev, umr_modify_atomic_disabled))
 		return false;
 
-	if (access_flags & IB_ACCESS_RELAXED_ORDERING)
+	if (access_flags & IB_ACCESS_RELAXED_ORDERING &&
+	    (MLX5_CAP_GEN(dev->mdev, relaxed_ordering_write) ||
+	     MLX5_CAP_GEN(dev->mdev, relaxed_ordering_read)))
 		return false;
 
 	return true;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/mlx5_ib.h`**
   - The condition for disabling UMR (User Memory Registration) usage has been modified. 
   - The original check only considered the presence of the `IB_ACCESS_RELAXED_ORDERING` flag. 
   - The new check now also verifies if the device has relaxed ordering capabilities (either for writing or reading) before disabling UMR. 
   - Specifically, the line:
     ```c
     if (access_flags & IB_ACCESS_RELAXED_ORDERING)
     ```
     has been changed to:
     ```c
     if (access_flags & IB_ACCESS_RELAXED_ORDERING &&
         (MLX5_CAP_GEN(dev->mdev, relaxed_ordering_write) ||
          MLX5_CAP_GEN(dev->mdev, relaxed_ordering_read)))
     ```

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `mlx5_ib.h` directly addresses a bug related to the handling of UMR when the relaxed ordering access flag is set. 
- By allowing UMR usage when the user requests relaxed ordering but the device lacks the necessary capabilities, the patch prevents unnecessary registration of a new memory key (mkey). 
- This change improves the efficiency of memory registration by ensuring that UMR can still be utilized in scenarios where relaxed ordering is requested but not supported, thus enhancing the overall functionality of the RDMA/mlx5 driver.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the incorrect handling of user memory registration (UMR) when the relaxed ordering access flag is used. The original implementation disabled UMR usage solely based on the presence of the relaxed ordering flag, without considering whether the device supports relaxed ordering capabilities. This oversight led to unnecessary mkey registrations when the requested access mode was not supported by the hardware.
